text: He opens by saying that hair loss is very common and that many people struggle with it.
He mentions treatments such as PRP and platelet-based procedures that people may try for hair loss.
He also mentions mesotherapy and minoxidil among commonly used approaches.
He says these treatments may produce temporary results but often require ongoing use.
He argues that hair loss may fundamentally relate to nutritional deficiencies and problems affecting the skin and scalp.
He mentions substances such as squalene and cholesterol while describing what he believes the scalp needs nutritionally.
He says hair loss should not be treated only with topical or temporary measures.
He claims that people with this problem may also show signs of peripheral nerve dysfunction, such as tingling in the hands.
He also mentions numbness and abnormal sensations of cold or heat in the limbs.
He says intolerance to cold extremities may appear alongside hair loss in some people; this is his clinical interpretation.
He concludes by recommending a dietary approach that removes some foods and increases others, according to the Al-Tayyibat system.
